A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REVIVE research. Their complete main texts and appendices A-G, including equations, figures and tables, support reliable comparison despite additions and reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original spectral reconstruction and perturbation experiments, sequential knowledge-editing results, general-ability evaluations and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds weight-norm measurements in Table 2 and MEND sequential-editing experiments in Table 8.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same SVD-based update representation, energy-threshold subspace selection and coefficient-filtering rule. Testing the existing wrapper with MEND introduces no new REVIVE component.

E1.justification: CounterFact, ZSRE and the general-ability task coverage are retained. MMLU already appears in v1 Appendix C.5 and Figure 17; its new Figure 16 comparison adds results rather than dataset coverage. RTE remains in Figure 9.

E2.justification: v1 discusses MEND without evaluating it. v2 Appendix G.7 and Table 8 add a paired MEND versus MEND+REVIVE comparison on GPT-J, extending evaluated editors to a meta-learning method. Existing main and DeltaEdit comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate MEND protocol with batch size 1 and checkpoints at 1, 50, 100, 500 and 1,000 edits. It also measures GPT-J layer-3 L1/L2 norms every 2,000 CounterFact edits through 10,000. Existing editing protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds a weight-norm trajectory analysis testing whether REVIVE suppresses parameter inflation during MEMIT editing. The existing perturbation, spectral-drift, threshold-sensitivity, t-SNE and extended-editing analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables retain their values after renumbering. New Table 2 reports 10,000-edit L2 norms of 20,946.66 for MEMIT versus 163.47 with REVIVE. New Table 8 reports 1,000-edit ZSRE efficacy of 0.00% for MEND versus 81.20% with REVIVE. Figure 16 adds MMLU comparison curves. These are newly reported results, not revisions to earlier performance values.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations and Appendix B theorem and proof are retained. Adding 'Frobenius' to the low-rank subspace similarity description clarifies its existing formula without changing the definition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the spectral-collapse explanation and plug-and-play REVIVE claims, including benefits under up to 20,000 edits. The added experiments support already-stated claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: v2 links dominant-subspace protection to suppressed weight-norm inflation and interprets MEND results as supporting applicability across editor families. A new limitation acknowledges that emerging evaluation metrics questioning existing protocols were not tested; the previous limitations remain.

D1.justification: Documentation for the added experiments specifies MEND's batch size and edit checkpoints and identifies GPT-J layer 3 for norm monitoring. Appendix C.6's GPU assignments, 10% protection threshold and torch.linalg.svd procedure, together with existing runtime measurements, remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds seven cited works: three Zhang et al. editing papers, Gupta and Xu papers supporting the norm-growth discussion, and two Liu papers motivating evaluation limitations. The central positioning against existing subspace-constrained editors remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized wording and spacing corrections accompany the norm-analysis paragraph, MEND subsection, acknowledgements, LLM-use disclosure and additional limitation. Most exposition and section ordering are retained; the runtime subsection moves from G.7 to G.8.

P2.justification: v2 adds norm Table 2 and MEND Table 8 and replaces Figure 16(b)'s duplicated RTE panel with an MMLU plot and corresponding axis labels. Retained tables and figures are redistributed and renumbered, while their visual designs and the overall two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: The MEND experiment strengthens evidence for REVIVE's applicability across editor families, the norm analysis adds a complementary diagnostic, and Figure 16 supplies the previously missing MMLU comparison. The new evaluation limitation also clarifies the evidence's scope. These are incremental gains: the method and principal results remain unchanged, and the added MEND and norm experiments cover only GPT-J without uncertainty estimates.
